minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Municipal Building Design Committee reviewed a space-needs spreadsheet comparing today's town hall/Ritter building footprint to 2016 and 2020 proposals, and leaned toward an open 'bullpen' layout with shared counters for departments like assessors, treasurer/collector and town clerk. Members debated whether to spend committee funds on hiring an architect for preliminary concept drawings versus attempting a first layout themselves, and a member argued strongly that TC Pacios (its storage, voting function, and community activities like the food pantry and teen center) must be folded into the committee's charge before any town hall/Ritter plan can succeed. The chair set the next meeting for July 20th and plans to press the select board to formally include TC Pacios in the committee's scope at its July 14th meeting.

what_happened.line: Committee leaned toward an open 'bullpen' office layout for town hall/Ritter, not separate department offices.
A member pushed to add the TC Pacios building -- storage, voting, food pantry, teen center -- to the committee's design charge.
Committee held off contacting an architect about paid concept work since he filed to run for select board.
Chair will ask the select board on July 14 to formally add TC Pacios to the committee's scope.

why_it_matters: This shapes the layout of a renovated or rebuilt town hall and whether the committee spends money hiring an outside architect.
Folding in TC Pacios would tie the food pantry, teen center, voting site and its storage into the same building plan and eventual funding request.
Holding off on the architect ties the design timeline to the outcome of the pending special election he is running in.
